name: graceful-shutdown-draining-p5
prompt: how do I stop my service without killing requests that are still in flight when it gets a shutdown signal

chunks.content: every config change is appended to an immutable audit trail with the actor and timestamp
preload the country list into memory at boot so the first dropdown render is fast
migrated the spacing scale to design tokens so padding is consistent across cards
ran the pending migration adding a nullable phone column to the accounts table
decided that on SIGTERM the server stops accepting new connections but keeps serving the requests already being handled until they finish, then exits
give in-progress handlers a 25-second grace window to complete during shutdown; anything still running past that is forcibly cut and logged
transactional emails that bounce are requeued twice before being parked for manual review
put the redesigned checkout behind a flag defaulting off until QA signs off
before draining begins we flip the readiness probe to failing so the load balancer pulls the instance out of rotation and no fresh traffic arrives
ship p95 and p99 latency histograms to the metrics backend on a 15-second scrape
an admin can forcibly terminate a user's active login session, which signs them out everywhere and revokes their tokens immediately
if the watchdog notices the process is wedged it escalates from a normal signal to SIGKILL, which kills it instantly with no cleanup
store all event times in UTC and localize only at render time
the background worker checks a stop flag between jobs so a long-running export is allowed to finish cleanly rather than being interrupted mid-write
